title: HC Mike LaFleur Press Conference: November 11 | Week 10 vs. Los Angeles Rams
headline: Carson Beck makes his first NFL start Sunday vs. the Rams after Gardner Minshew's season-ending injury, with Michael Wilson also out for the year.
summary: LaFleur confirmed that Carson Beck will start at quarterback this week. Gardner Minshew is having surgery and is done for the season, though the coach did not know the exact procedure. Michael Wilson is on season-ending IR, but LaFleur said the long-term prognosis is good and he did not know the return timeline. Beck will take 100% of the first-team reps and already knows the receivers from running scout team with them. LaFleur praised Beck's maturity, his improved footwork and his comfort in the huddle and under center, and said he has no expectations beyond playing one play at a time. He also pointed to the receiver and tight end rooms as places where depth players get a chance to step up. On the offensive line, Jon Gaines is out of practice today with an ankle but trending well and is still undecided for Sunday, and Hjalte Froholdt is in the concussion protocol. The team signed veteran Josh Johnson, who will back up Beck.

injuries.detail: Season-ending knee/UCL-type injury per reporters; LaFleur said he will have surgery but did not know the exact procedure. He suffered it on the last play of the first half and played into the second half.
On season-ending IR. The prognosis is good and it should not affect him going forward, but LaFleur did not know the return date (OTAs or later).

signals.quote: Carson will be the starter.

signals.note: He is off the fantasy radar for the year, and Beck takes over as the starter.

topics.detail: LaFleur called the injuries a big opportunity for the receiver room, which has only about five total catches among the group coaches mentioned, and for the tight ends to step up even more. He did not name specific players.
The team signed Josh Johnson, whom LaFleur has known since 2020, to back up Beck. A young quarterback named Joey was also brought in, and LaFleur said the team had liked him since the draft process.

Beck gets 100% of the reps this week and is familiar with the receivers from scout team. LaFleur said he has gotten quieter with his feet and understands the timing of the offense. LaFleur said Beck will not be scared to let it rip.
LaFleur said the front office kept the roster intact, and he is focused on coaching up the 53 plus the practice squad, reminding players that they are one snap away from playing.

title: HC Kevin Stefanski on preparations to take on Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs | Press Conference
headline: Falcons traded Jessie Bates III and C Ryan Neuzil, Brian Robinson is on IR after a setback, and Khalil Herbert is trusted as Bijan Robinson's backup, with Corey Levin stepping in at center vs. KC.
summary: Stefanski opened by calling the Chiefs a big challenge and praised Andy Reid's staff and the roster. Most questions were about the trade deadline moves: Ryan Neuzil (a captain) and Jessie Bates III were traded, which he framed as best for the team now. He said Corey Levin, a veteran center who has been with the team since the spring, will step in, and new lineman Andrew Vorhees will be brought up to speed by the offensive line coaches. Brian Robinson went on IR after a setback at practice, and Stefanski said the team trusts Khalil Herbert to carry the backup RB load. He defended Michael Penix Jr. on turnovers and pressure, saying he's an accurate passer and won't be told simply not to turn it over. He also said a new kicker, Jake Moody, will be evaluated this week after Nick Folk's departure. He downplayed Kyle Pitts' production by saying the whole offense is short of where it wants to be. He declined to speculate on Patrick Mahomes' health, praised Kenneth Walker, and said penalties will get extra emphasis. He rejected any focus on draft position or long-term thinking.

title: Jesse Minter on Kicker Situation, Jacoby Brissett's First Practice
headline: Jacoby Brissett is the new Ravens QB for Monday night vs. the Chargers, with the kicker spot still open and Jaylinn Hawkins a possible return.
summary: Minter opened by saying the team is a day ahead of schedule for Monday night against the Chargers. The team used the extra time for a recap and self-scout, and installed some new offensive ideas. He said Jacoby Brissett, in his first days with the team, has a commanding presence, runs the huddle and will help young receivers, linemen and tight ends. He expects the offensive coordinator, Declan, to build a game plan around Brissett's strengths, as he did after the quarterback changes earlier this season. The kicker spot is unsettled: Minter said more kickers will work out, and Jake Moody had a chance to join but chose to go elsewhere. Newly acquired lineman Ryan Neuzil adds depth and positional flexibility, but Minter does not expect any change for Cam Jurgens, whom he called the future of the line. On defense, he wants better coverage tied to the pass rush and better finishing on sacks and strip attempts. Jaylinn Hawkins was back on the field, and Minter will judge over the next day or two whether he can play Monday. Minter also praised Justin Herbert's talent and said facing his former team will be fun but competitive.

injuries.detail: Back on the practice field. The team will see how he responds over the next day or two before deciding if he can play Monday.

signals.note: His job looks secure and the line's alignment should stay stable as a new QB arrives.

topics.detail: Jacoby Brissett has been added and is already leading in walkthroughs and meetings. Minter expects the coordinator to build a plan Brissett is comfortable with, drawing on similarities to systems he has run before.

Ryan Neuzil was acquired at the deadline as a versatile depth piece who may move between positions. Minter does not see him displacing Cam Jurgens.
Minter wants better finishing on sacks and strip attempts, and tighter coverage tied to the rush. He said better coverage makes the quarterback hold the ball longer, which lets the rush produce.
Minter praised Declan's poise after the team had to go to a third quarterback early in a game and then prepare a short-week plan. He expects the same adjustment now.

Minter called Herbert extremely talented, with elite arm talent and athleticism. He noted that Herbert is learning another new offense, probably his fifth or sixth coordinator, and said it has not yet clicked. Minter also said facing his former team will be competitive but fun.

title: Joe Brady Talks The Addition of Amani Hooker And Facing The New York Jets
headline: Bills added S Amani Hooker, but his Sunday status at the Jets depends on how fast he learns the playbook. CB Christian Benford (left Monday's game) has no update until Friday.
summary: Joe Brady is excited about Amani Hooker, whom he called a savvy, cerebral safety who finds the football and should pick up the system quickly. Whether Hooker plays Sunday on the road depends on how much he can process and communicate, and the team will take it day by day. Brady pushed back on the idea that the trade shows doubt in Damar Hamlin. He said Hamlin has earned his role and will keep a defensive and special teams role. He said the move adds versatility and depth, and that Cole Bishop has been playing well and needs to build communication with Hooker. Brady called the Jets one of the most explosive offenses, with a deep-throwing Geno Smith, two strong running backs and a matchup-problem rookie tight end. He also praised edge rusher David Bailey. On injuries, Christian Benford, Dion Dawkins and one other player the captions render as 'Alec' are not doing full-speed work, and Brady hopes to have clearer answers Friday. He also praised Greg Dortch as a return spark regardless of his offensive snaps, and said the team is connected and not looking at the standings.

title: Dave Canales: 'I have a lot of confidence in this locker room'
headline: Bryce Young is off the injury report, and Jalen Coker, Michael Jackson, Jonathon Brooks and others are back at practice, but Canales says availability depends on Wednesday's practice and the RB rotation is unsettled.
summary: Canales said the team is excited about the divisional trip to New Orleans. Several injured players returned to a modified practice, and he said Thursday's session would test their durability before anyone is cleared for Sunday. Bobby Okereke did not practice (DNP) while working through a foot injury, and Canales called the next day big for him. Bryce Young is no longer on the injury report after a solid week, and Canales said he looked great and is doing his job. Jalen Coker is back after re-aggravating his hamstring, and Canales said the team pushed his rehab and he is driving it. Canales called the quiet trade deadline a mix of getting players back and cap and resource limits, and he named Xavier Legette, Jaycee Horn, Devin Lloyd and Jaelan Phillips as reinforcements. On defense, he said interim coordinator Todd's imprint is about play style first, and he told the corners to stay aggressive but be cleaner at the catch point. On the RB rotation behind Chuba Hubbard, he leaned on Trevor Etienne and said little about Jonathon Brooks's role. He expects the Saints to lean on zone running and to rush the passer well, so Carolina needs a balanced, efficient run game.

title: Zac Taylor Talks Injury Updates, Trade Deadline, White Bengal Game Against Steelers | PRESS CONFERENCE
headline: Bengals are 6-2 and stood pat at the deadline. Dylan Fairchild is on IR with no timetable, and Chase Brown has Zac Taylor's full confidence as a three-phase back, though a tough Steelers run defense limits his rushing ceiling.
summary: Taylor opened by saying Dylan Fairchild is on IR, day to day, with a timetable still to be determined, and that his return will go beyond the IR window. He confirmed the team is close to opening IR return windows for a couple of players, possibly this week. The Bengals tried to add edge depth at the deadline, but the cost was higher than expected and the deal fell through; Taylor said the team is happy with its roster and won't be distracted. A defensive end who had been on IR will fill the open roster spot. The team has just three quarterbacks after Josh Johnson left for Arizona, and Taylor still calls the room the NFL's best. For Sunday night's game against the 4-game-win-streak Steelers, Taylor called Pittsburgh's defense a great front and one of the best rush defenses in the league. He said the Bengals' heavy pass volume reflects his trust in the offensive line, and he praised Chase Brown's confidence and his work in rushing, protection and the pass game. He also praised slot corner Josh Newton for his energy and experience in the scheme. He joked off a question about Joe Burrow's limp, calling it 'swag', and he managed practice workload carefully, especially for the O-line, D-line and receivers.

title: Todd Monken Press Conference : November 11th, 2026
headline: Deshaun Watson stays the Browns' starting QB over Shedeur Sanders for the Texans game, though Monken calls it week to week. Denzel Boston is out of practice today with a toe issue but is expected back tomorrow.
summary: Monken confirmed Deshaun Watson as the starter, citing his body of work over the first eight games he played, and said the decision was always his intention. He framed it as neither a long-term commitment nor a strictly week-to-week call, but said he anticipates Watson remaining the starter. He praised Shedeur Sanders for staying ready after about ten weeks of taking no reps, while saying both quarterbacks have plenty of room to improve. Monken was frustrated by the team's penalties (32nd in the league, mostly pre-snap and mostly up front) but said he will not change the starting offensive line or other starters. He rejected the idea of a short-yardage problem, calling the red-zone and fourth-down trouble an execution issue. On injuries, Ronnie Hickman is in concussion protocol after the game, and Denzel Boston has a minor toe issue, sat out today and is expected back tomorrow. He called Houston's defense very tough, praising the edge rushers (including Clowney) and talent at all three levels. He said protecting against that pass rush limits his play-calling options. He also played down a viral clip about Sanders suggesting plays outside the playbook and rejected the idea of leaning on the hurry-up offense to fix slow starts.

He has no answer for the slow starts beyond continued work. He is wary of leaning on the hurry-up or throwing 50 times a game, and wants the run game to work when needed.

Monken said edge rushers like Will Anderson and Clowney change how an offense schemes and which pass concepts it can use. Last week the team had to keep an extra blocker in (possibly TE Harold Fannin Jr., per the reporter's garbled question), and that could happen again.
Monken called the viral clip about Sanders suggesting plays outside the playbook a normal, lighthearted day-to-day conversation between quarterback and coach, not a big deal.
Monken said the game is a big AFC matchup in which Cleveland is fighting to get to six wins.

He credited the recent run of 12 sacks in four games to Mike Pettine's voice, individual pass-rush wins by Quinnen Williams and Kenny Clark, and more blitzes. He called San Francisco a great team in all three phases, with a fast-processing Brock Purdy, a quick-rhythm passing game, elite run-after-catch players and heavy use of motion. He stressed protecting the ball and tackling well. On injuries, Ferguson and Goodson won't practice, Mingo will do little, and Jalen Thompson is still out. Malik Hooker was excused for a personal matter, and Joey Porter Jr.'s availability is still unclear. James Mitchell has been 'incredible' filling in for Ferguson, while Trigg is a good route runner who still needs to improve his blocking. Javonte Williams got strong praise as the run game returns to balance.

Kyler Murray has only just started a running progression for his hamstring strain, is week-to-week, and is projected as a DNP on the first report. Carson Wentz has a minor ankle injury and is projected as limited, and O'Connell hopes he can be the No. 2 QB. Max Brosmer got praise for his late-game work on Monday night. O'Connell said there is no in-season quarterback competition, but he believes in Murray, Wentz and Brosmer as depth once Murray is healthy. He also wants to build Cousins' workload progressively rather than ask too much early, with the goal of playing best football in December. Blake Cashman is in the concussion protocol after the stinger evaluation and a late hit in the Monday night game. The team is 6-2 but has struggled on offense for two straight weeks, and Green Bay is playing very well.

topics.detail: Saleh said the Hooker trade, like the earlier 'Jeff' trade, was unfortunate but necessary because a losing team gets offers it can't refuse. He compared it to a next-man-up situation and said he will let the locker room decide on new captains.

He said the last two games were well below standard, but the busts and open receivers in zone coverage have decreased considerably. He said the defense still needs to win more one-on-ones, rush the passer better and tackle better.
At 1-7, Saleh said he is disappointed and that there is no timeline for success. He said the goal is to get better every day and to finish the final nine games strong.

He called Jacksonville a top-ten unit in all three phases that develops its young talent well. He said Trevor Lawrence is playing the best football of his career and that the defense's three additions make them better.
